item.title: In a world full of noise, the brands that feel human stay with us
item.description: Most brands today are trying very hard to be noticed. Louder campaigns, sharper taglines, bigger promises. But if you think about the brands you actually remember, they’re rarely the ones shouting the most. They’re the ones that feel familiar. Every brand, whether it sells milk, paint, or technology services, is speaking to a person. And people don’t make decisions like machines. They rely on habit, comfort, emotion, and what feels right at that moment. In India especially, trust builds slowly.

item.title: Dabur reports 5.3% YoY growth in ad spends in Q3 FY26
item.description: Dabur India increased its advertising and promotion spends by 5.3% year-on-year to Rs 238 crore in Q3 FY26, underlining its focus on boosting demand and market share. Last year, it stood at Rs 226.7 crore, while in the previous quarter it was Rs 233.6 crore. The higher investment coincided with improved financial performance. item.title: BharatPe rolls out ‘Super Over’ campaign with Rohit Sharma ahead of T20 World Cup
item.description: BharatPe has launched a new nationwide campaign titled ‘Super Over’, featuring Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma, ahead of the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup. The initiative seeks to link everyday UPI transactions with India’s widespread engagement with cricket. The campaign includes a brand film that draws parallels between high-pressure moments in cricket and routine payment scenarios.
